component: Git SHA reference (final git SHA vs HEAD)

observed_ground_truth: Ground truth's HEAD is `c427cd97ca8187ed2349984c87b6562eaf7e7d07`, matching all watchdog runs and job receipts (EV002, EV005).
expected_ground_truth: The claim's short SHA `f2d7c75` cannot be matched or ruled out against the full HEAD SHA from the evidence bundle; there is no direct evidence confirming f2d7c75 is an ancestor or equal to c427cd9.

suggested_next_step: Run `git log --oneline | grep f2d7c75` or `git merge-base --is-ancestor f2d7c75 HEAD` on the VPS to confirm the claimed SHA is part of current history.

component: Working tree cleanliness vs claim of committed/pushed state
claim: Final git SHA: f2d7c75, pushed to origin/main, pulled and verified on the VPS ... frozen registries and holdout lock verified unchanged via git status (only the two report/state modules + two new supporting modules touched)
observed_ground_truth: Ground truth shows the working tree is NOT clean at HEAD c427cd9 -- numerous modified tracked files and many untracked files/directories are present (EV002), with no evidence explaining whether these are expected runtime artifacts or unreviewed code.
expected_ground_truth: The claim implies a clean, verified git state ('git status' checked, only specific modules touched) consistent with a fully committed and pushed change set, but the ground truth working tree shows broader uncommitted changes than described.
operational_impact: If untracked/modified files beyond the claimed 'two report/state modules + two new supporting modules' exist, the audit trail for what was actually verified/pushed is incomplete or inconsistent.
suggested_next_step: Run `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --stat HEAD` on the VPS and compare the file list against the four modules named in the claim.
